bullets.title: April JOLTS 9-sigma beat: job openings surge to 7.62M vs 6.87M est
bullets.body: April JOLTS job openings printed 7.618M vs consensus 6.866M—a roughly 750K beat described as a 9-sigma event and the largest positive deviation in JOLTS history. The vacancy-to-unemployment ratio rose above 1.0 to the highest since January 2025, while quits fell to a 6-year low of 1.9% and hires declined to 3.2%, creating a puzzling divergence between demand-side openings and worker confidence. The surge was concentrated in professional and business services, which saw its largest-ever jump in openings.

bullets.title: Fed's Hammack signals rate hikes may be needed 'soon' if inflation doesn't cool
bullets.body: Cleveland Fed President Hammack stated that monetary policy may not be tight enough to lower inflation and that the Fed might need to act 'soon' if recent trends continue. She flagged growing risk of persistent inflation pressures as her primary concern, warning that delayed action could require larger adjustments at greater cost. Separately, BoE's Greene said the case for rate hikes is growing as the Iran conflict drags on, arguing that acting quickly has benefits and that the risk of inaction exceeds premature tightening.

bullets.title: Eurozone May CPI hits 3.2%, highest since 2023; ECB rate-hike path complicated
bullets.body: Eurozone headline inflation rose to 3.2% in May (up from 3.0% in April), with core at 2.5% and services jumping to 3.5% from 3.0%—the highest reading since 2023 and driven in part by the Middle East energy shock. Multiple sources flagged this complicates the ECB's easing path and may cement a rate-hike move.

bullets.title: BofA sees rising US reflation odds through 2027-28; limited upside in peak yields
bullets.body: Bank of America expects a US reflation mini-cycle lasting through 2027–2028, supported by recent macro data, but sees limited upside to peak Treasury yields. JPM upgraded its Q2 2026 GDP forecast to 2.5% from 1.5%, noting S&P 500 earnings are more tied to nominal GDP than real GDP, mapping the inflationary impulse to improved earnings rather than margin compression. The 10-year yield faces material resistance at 4.35–4.40% (Apr 61.8% retracement / 50-DMA), with support at the 4.56% May 26 gap.

bullets.title: S&P on 9-day winning streak, up 10.7% YTD—approaching historically rare territory
bullets.body: SPY was tracking its 9th consecutive up-day, tying a historical record, as the index has gained 10.7% through the first five months of 2026—on pace for a fourth straight 15%+ annual return, a feat last achieved in the 1995–1999 streak. Ned Davis Research raised its 2026 year-end S&P target to 7,950. However, JPM's 1-Delta desk flagged clear signs of retail excess, Goldman noted negative advance-decline breadth during the 5-day rally, and Barclays warned the AI-driven rally is vulnerable to correction. SPY was pinned near 759 with a large 2B net GEX call wall at the 760 strike.

bullets.title: Alphabet announces $80B equity raise; market reads it as AI capex stress signal
bullets.body: Alphabet announced a $30B secondary offering (split between mandatory convertible preferred shares and Class A/C common stock) plus a $10B private placement to Berkshire Hathaway at ~$350/share, totaling ~$80B raised for AI infrastructure. GOOGL fell 3.9% on the news. Goldman's equity supply analysis showed this swing net Q4-25 equity issuance from -$44B to +$40B, while BofA argued it will pressure investors to sell recent winners to fund new shares. Oppenheimer noted equity issuance (vs debt) signals a less favorable AI data center financing environment; Goldman simultaneously raised its 2026 IPO volume forecast to $225B from $160B.

bullets.title: Iran-US deal odds collapse to 27%; Hormuz blockade and oil spike persist
bullets.body: Kalshi markets saw US-Iran deal probability fall from ~75% to 27% during the window, with Strait of Hormuz reopening probability at just 22% and normal shipping odds at 52% by October 2026. The US has redirected 122 commercial vessels due to the blockade, global shipping costs have more than doubled since February, and WTI reversed losses to trade near $92/barrel. Trump denied reports of halted talks and Rubio set Hormuz opening as Condition #1 for negotiations, while Hezbollah rejected any partial ceasefire and Lebanon announced a partial truce. The UAB Barakah nuclear plant suffered an attack causing external power loss.

bullets.title: Trump signs AI executive order; government gets pre-launch access to frontier models
bullets.body: Trump signed an executive order promoting AI innovation and security, mandating government early access to 'frontier models' prior to public launch and establishing a classified AI benchmarking process. DoD and DHS must expedite cyber defense of civilian federal systems within 30 days; DoC will lead an AI cybersecurity clearinghouse. Systems software analysts flagged CRWD and PANW as best-positioned for the resulting federal cyber budget grab via FedRAMP pathways and incident response franchises. Companies with most FedRAMP authorizations—IBM, OKTA, CRWD, PANW, CyberArk—positioned for immediate access to new OMB/CISA grant funding.

bullets.title: Memory 'Chipflation': AI demand creating durable supply-demand reset, not cycle
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Chipflation report warns AI demand has pushed memory prices up ~6x over the past year across HBM, DRAM, and enterprise SSDs, and the cycle looks structurally different from prior semiconductor upcycles. Hyperscalers are locking capacity via LTAs and prepayments, leaving tighter supply for traditional buyers; smartphone/PC memory supply is expected to fall 12–15% short despite 30% capacity expansion by 2027. Memory producers (Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron/WDC/Seagate) benefit; consumer hardware OEMs face elevated cost exposure. SK Hynix separately announced plans to double capacity over five years, and MLCC supply is described as the tightest in 25 years.

bullets.title: Data center construction: 60% of 102GW pipeline at risk; only ~40GW likely by 2030
bullets.body: Jefferies-Sightline analysis found ~60% of announced data center projects through 2030 face material risk from power procurement delays, permitting, and EPC execution constraints. Of 102GW announced, only ~40GW is assessed as likely to materialize; 13GW is already delayed, dominated by Fermi America's 11GW HyperGrid Campus. ~50GW of the 2027–2028 pipeline comes from inexperienced developers, and off-grid projects face larger operational and financing constraints than perceived. Data center construction spending itself surpassed $50B for the first time, widening its lead over general office construction.

bullets.title: Gold overtakes US Treasuries as world's top reserve asset at 27% vs 22%
bullets.body: ECB data confirmed gold's share of total official foreign reserves reached 27% at end-2025, overtaking US Treasuries at 22% and euro holdings at 15%—the first time gold has topped the reserve leaderboard. Multiple macro commentators flagged this as a structural shift away from USD-denominated assets.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley: AI infrastructure spend tracking ~10x early cloud cycle; $256T available capital
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley noted AI infrastructure spending is already running ~10x above where early cloud cycle spend was at a comparable stage, with approximately $256 trillion of global capital theoretically available to finance the buildout. The bank separately argues the AI investment boom creates a durable supply-demand reset in memory and cross-sector margin pressure via PPI effects, while Goldman Sachs warned AI will widen the competitive gap between corporate giants and smaller competitors.

bullets.title: OpenAI CFO: compute demand exceeds capacity through 2027; enterprise now 50% of revenue
bullets.body: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar said on the All-In podcast that AI compute demand will exceed available capacity through at least 2026–2027 across power, land, chips, memory, and talent. 1 GW of capacity supports ~$10B of annual revenue; OpenAI is building a 1 GW Michigan data center. Enterprise revenue is now ~50% of total; ChatGPT has 900M+ weekly users and ~11% search market share. Model efficiency costs fell ~97% from GPT-4 to GPT-5.4-class. OpenAI is diversifying chip supply beyond NVIDIA to AMD, Broadcom, and Cerebras, and cloud beyond Azure to Oracle, Google, AWS, and CoreWeave. IPO is not a near-term priority after the recent $122B fundraising round.

bullets.title: Microsoft Build 2026: custom silicon, AI agents, edge compute dominate keynote
bullets.body: Microsoft Build showcased Maia 200 delivering 30% better cost/token vs standard GPUs (now powering M365 Copilot), Cobalt 200 ARM-based CPU showing 33% latency/23% throughput gains, and the Surface RTX Spark DevBox with 128GB unified memory and 1 PF local compute. Azure AI revenue hit $37B (+123% YoY) with RPO of $627B (+99% YoY); the company is on pace to double cloud capacity in two years. New products include Foundry IQ (enterprise knowledge layer), Project Solara (OS for AI agent devices), AION reasoning models, and Rayfin (AI-agent BaaS). MSFT also announced a Mayo Clinic strategic collaboration to develop a frontier AI healthcare model.

bullets.title: Semis rip: MRVL +32.5% after Jensen calls it next $1T company; SOX +5.9%
bullets.body: The SOX semi index surged 5.9% as Jensen Huang called Marvell a potential next trillion-dollar company at Computex, with MRVL closing up 32.5% and up another 18% the following morning (57% in two weeks). NVIDIA committed $2B to Marvell; the companies jointly framed AI infrastructure as transitioning from a compute/memory bottleneck to a connectivity bottleneck, with optical interconnect as the next critical upgrade cycle. MRVL traders were described as 'unshortable' ahead of a potential S&P 500 inclusion announcement. COHR, LITE, GLW, FN, VIAV, CIEN all surged 10%+ on optical tailwinds.

bullets.title: JPM maintains tactical bullish stance; upgrades Q2 GDP to 2.5%; key hedge: energy longs, VIX, puts
bullets.body: JPM's afternoon briefing maintained a tactical bullish stance on equities and upgraded its Q2 2026 GDP forecast to 2.5% from 1.5%, noting nominal GDP growth is supporting earnings despite inflationary costs. Desk recommends staying long AI theme and Mag 7 while adding hedges via energy longs, VIX longs, and index puts. Key risks cited: tariff resumption in July, Iran conflict escalation, and factor pullbacks in Beta and Momentum. Cyclicals (Airlines +19.1%, Retailers +10.2%, Homebuilders +6.6% since May 15) are now at risk if energy prices spike. Non-profitable tech is back to 2021 levels; software (IGV) is 25% above its 50-DMA.

bullets.title: Retail options at most bullish since 2021 meme craze; Goldman flags excess
bullets.body: CBOE data showed retail opening options activity at its most bullish level since the 1H 2021 meme-stock era. Goldman's 1-Delta desk simultaneously flagged 'clear signs of excess' in retail participation. Breadth has been negative during the past five up-days in the S&P—a potential distribution signal. Credit vol significantly outperformed equity vol during the Iran geopolitical event; Morgan Stanley's credit desk noted ATM vols near historical lows with skew screening steep, with fast money selling HY vol (particularly 25-delta payers out to Sep).

bullets.title: SpaceX IPO targets $1.75T valuation; roadshow starts Thursday
bullets.body: SpaceX announced its IPO roadshow begins Thursday with a $1.75T valuation target (including greenshoe), down from earlier $2T+ aspirations. Banks are expected to earn $500M in fees; SpaceX is negotiating to cut those fees below 0.75%. Morningstar values SpaceX at $780B (~48% below IPO target), assigning a Narrow Moat. Goldman raised its 2026 IPO volume forecast to $225B from $160B, and equity supply analysts flagged potential selling pressure from $500B in expiring lockups.

bullets.title: Medicare to cover GLP-1 drugs at $50/month; European Parliament switching Google search to Qwant
bullets.body: CMS Administrator Dr. Oz announced Medicare eligible beneficiaries can obtain GLP-1 products at a $50/month starting price. Separately, the European Parliament plans to switch from Google to Qwant for search services, signaling incremental institutional customer pressure on Alphabet.

bullets.title: Henry Huang effect: Semis co-design reduces future cyclicality; memory now structural not cyclical
bullets.body: Multiple semiconductor analysts argued the AI infrastructure cycle is fundamentally different from prior semi cycles: MLCC supply is the tightest in 25 years, co-design ecosystems are eliminating traditional digestion troughs, and the memory market is entering a structural repricing rather than a normal upturn. Hyperscalers are committing to LTAs and prepayments through 2027+, with customers (not just suppliers) driving long-term wafer agreements past 2029. Arrow Electronics and Avnet both reported backlogs 50–80% higher YoY and positive book-to-bill across all regions.
